options.text: The third interior angle is $180^{\circ}-71^{\circ}=109^{\circ}$, ignoring $44^{\circ}$.
The third interior angle equals the exterior angle at the same vertex.

teacher.key_rationale: Interior angles sum to 180°, so the missing angle is 180°−(71°+44°)=65°. Adding the two known angles substitutes the wrong operation. Dropping 44° omits a given angle. Equating to an exterior angle leaves this interior-sum hinge.

stem:
Omar knows two interior angles of a triangle are $71^{\circ}$ and $44^{\circ}$. He wants the third interior angle.

Which claim is correct?
